reuse.why: All six month-wide actions share category selection and reuse existing budget, spreadsheet, batching, and undo helpers, although income eligibility remains repeated.

duplication.why: The repeated category queries are consolidated, but the new spending action adds another copy of the income-versus-tracking eligibility guard.

placement.why: Selection policy and budget operations remain in budget/actions.ts, with typed method registration and mutation wrappers in budget/app.ts.

scope.why: The changes are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their registration, focused tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared selector gives future exclusions one clear home, though its return type overstates the selected group fields and income eligibility remains distributed.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every affected month-wide action calls getMonthWideCategories, and the new action uses the existing budget mutation and undo abstractions.

disguised_duplication.where: Repeated category-selection queries are replaced by shared calls; the remaining income guard is straightforward repetition rather than disguised logic.

abstraction_drift.where: getMonthWideCategories gains the requested includeHiddenCategories parameter and its conditional SQL filter; all six consumers pass the flag directly without bypassing the selector.
